newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei end higher but bearish mood persists.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei end higher but bearish mood persists.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished firmer on Friday, helped by the dollar's rise against the yen and Wall Street's upbeat tone overnight, but dealers said gains were on thin volumes and the market could head south again.
"This might be a bit of a technical bounce, but I still prefer to stay short," a trader at a U.S. futures house said.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract added 155 points to end at 19,430, 30 points below its day high. Market volume was a thin 10,830 lots.
Dealers said the contract's failure to approach a band of resistance at 19,500-19,600 suggested further gains would be difficult.
Taiwan stock index futures ended firmer as Taipei shares surged after the government approved a "two-into-one" tax merger plan to boost the island's investment and economy.
The Taiwan cabinet agreed to merge the island's two income taxes into one business income tax, with effect from 1998, in a move to avoid double taxation and help corporate structures.
A rally in computer-related shares on hopes of continued strong sales also boosted Taiwan stocks.
The August MSCI Taiwan index contract ended up 3.2 to 405.3 on volume of 2,561 lots.
